anomalies.obs: On the Power sheet the MIC26903 feedback divider from the FB pin (NET0107) to the +5V output is R53 = 6k8 (top) with R60 = 19k6 (bottom, FB-to-GND); the 1k3 resistor R12 is instead tied as a bleeder from the output node to GND. With Vref = 0.8 V this divider gives Vout = 0.8*(1+6.8/19.6) ≈ 1.1 V, not 5 V.
anomalies.expected: The rail is specified and labelled +5 V (block diagram '9A @ 5V max'; the sheet note 'Vout=0.8*(1+R5/R6)'). To obtain 5 V the FB-to-GND resistor must be ≈1.3 kΩ (i.e. the value currently on R12), so R60's value is wrong / R60 and R12 appear swapped.

evidence.quote: 5 V rail: MIC26903YJL-TR ... 'Vout=0.8*(1+R5/R6)' ... Block diagram caption: '9A @ 5V max.'

anomalies.impact: The buck would regulate to roughly 1 V instead of 5 V. The +5V rail (servo/PWM bank, USB VBUS, GPS) would collapse and the LD39200 3.3 V LDO could not produce 3.3 V, so the MCUs and sensors would not power up.

parsed.summary: The drawing supports one anomaly: the MIC26903 feedback divider (R53 6k8 / R60 19k6) cannot produce the specified +5 V rail, indicating a wrong divider resistor value (R60 should be ~1.3 kΩ, as R12). Other documented differences (baro RESET/EOC swap, PCA9685 strapped to 0x41 to avoid the INA219 0x40 conflict) are intended design properties, not anomalies.
